- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 30d mean.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–4% if sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.5 to +0.3 within 5 days), model often lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to hold or overestimate; apply downward bias of 1–3% per day of deviation.  
- For 30d forecasts, if model’s first 5 days are consistently above true outcome, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day starting from day 6.  
- If sentiment is positive but price drops sharply (e.g., +0.3 then -0.5), model often ignores sentiment; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment decay by reducing 1–2% per day after sentiment flip.
